items.note: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green; Gideon Vose first president to 1911; creamery built 1891 (Story 1)
Article VII quoted verbatim, both halves including 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern' (Story 1)
Falke cited: under payment by weight nothing that followed would have cost any man a dollar (Story 1)
Loomis secretary 1901; Teague bookkeeper from 1905 (Story 7); Sill weighing into his churn at Larrow Green (Story 7)
Section A never states Selby is Gideon's son nor manager from 1913; both appear only in Section B/D, and Section A credit does not travel from B-G
station gain line reproduced with the 1898 entry, 'one like it every year after', five and a quarter per cent, carried to the general account (Story 7)
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green (Story 2)
full bench routine: weighing, composite ten-day sample, fixed charge from the measure, fat read in percent; cream down, skim home (Story 2)
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897 (Story 3)
invoice reproduced in full: 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, total 77.93 (Story 3)
'the Ostrey Hollow gap stood flat at nineteen hundredths in July and in February, in wet years and dry' (Story 4)

the 'pipette is the plant's own standard and cannot be checked without a burette' argument is made only in Section F1; Section A says only that burettes were issued from 1921 and most plants never had it done
Ansel Keddie b.1861, tester twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934 (Stories 2, 8)
five-column test book (date, patron, pounds, test, fat), one hand, errors struck and initialed rather than written over (Story 2)
summary leaf: 1896 3.80; 1897 part year; 1898 3.61 and within three hundredths every year since (Story 2). Both figures present
8 May breakage, borrowed measure, 3.80 through the interval, back to 3.61 on 10 July, the question mark (Story 5)
'Orra Keddie was Emmet Brant's sister, and Emmet was the station's largest patron' (Story 6)
1919 circular over the manager's signature (Story 6); 17 March 1925 statement denying he took cream (Story 8) plus 'I could not answer it then and I cannot answer it now' (Story 5)
died February 1934 (bolded element of the item)
Hessel Bottom wet meadow, six farms with rights, Emmet Brant's the largest (Story 4)
Section A names Brant's weigh book only as exhibit 3 at the hearing; the 1 January 1897 start and the two scales agreeing appear only in Sections C and E

complaints from about 1902 that Hollow milk tested under valley milk (Story 4); the run also keeps the two gaps properly apart (0.17 Hollow-vs-Green at E7, 0.19 true shortfall), so the conflation penalty does not apply
1908 Grigg committee and its bog-hay finding stated as a finding (Story 4), but the bolded Jan/Feb/Mar 1908 sampling window appears only in Sections E and F, not inside Section A
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional-loss comparison with the 4.56 Vose Jerseys appear only in Sections C and F, never in Section A
no mention anywhere in Section A of the weigh book passing to Roy Brant in 1929 or being lent to Ivy Keddie in 1958
Jerome Cudd's cheese factory at Alder Corners, over Redlow Ridge, in Vessey County (Story 4) - all four gating elements; year does not gate
from 1915, four Hessel Bottom men hauled over in the summer flush, June to mid-September, Ostrey Hollow the rest of the year (Story 4)
REQUIRED met with all four: another county, his own bench, his own glass, never compared a figure with anybody's (Story 4)
same milk ran 3.78-3.82, about 3.80, season after season for sixteen seasons ending 1930 against the station's 3.61 (Story 4)
'The same milk, off the same wet ground' tested differently in two buildings, offered as one of the two things that kill the hay answer (Story 4)
Rosalie Cudd appears in Section A only as a bearing-documents line; daughter, 1941-1962, and copying sixteen seasons for Ivy in 1958 are all in Sections D and E
'Merle Strawn, on the Ordell circuit since 1907' (Story 8) - the contested start year taken correctly against the 1908 pair
'I have tested for water at this station on every visit I have made to it and I have never found any' (Story 6); 'Lactometer, no added water, as always here' (Story 8)
12 June 1923, pipettes run against the burette, whole crate condemned (Story 8)
'I did not weigh what it has cost them'; drew no inference about the twenty-six years behind it (Story 8)
ordered 28 June, answered 2 July, in use that July, 1924 average 3.80, and nobody connected the rise with the condemnation (Stories 3, 8)
crate went up the ladder into the loft over the intake room that June (Story 8) - the key assigns this item the 'where it went in 1923' aspect
'In January the Ostrey Hollow patrons petitioned' under the 1925 heading (Story 8); the date carries the item
board under Alonzo Frick, three sittings, 17 March at Ashlin and twice more in the station's weigh room, award 4 May (Story 8)
water (Vose), theft by the tester (Teague), wet hay (1908 report read in); 'None was proved' (Story 8)
four books named including the 1923 circuit notebook; 'Nobody laid the second beside the fourth' (Story 8)
dismissed 30 April, no cause established, $3,800 without admission charged to the station account, 4 May (Story 8)
Section A never states the award was one fifth of the $19,000 lost, nor identifies the station account with the account the 'gain' had been accumulating in; the fraction appears only at C1(d)
Ivy Keddie, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Vaught named on the bulletin (Story 8)
Section A never describes her assembling records that had never been in the same room; the nearest statement is the eight-records line in Section G
February 1958, crate found in the loft, nine unbroken pipettes (Story 8)
9 March, calibrated burette, five runs each, mean 16.72 against 17.6, 0.95 of the mark (Story 8)
components all present inside Section A: 0.95 of the mark (Story 8), 3.61 against a true 3.80 (Stories 2, 4, 5), flat nineteen hundredths (Story 4)
REQUIRED fails inside Section A: the 25-year span 1898-1922 is absent (only 1,600,000 lb a year at Story 7), and 76,000 lb, $19,000 and the ledger identity appear only in Sections C and G
Bulletin No. 471 in October 1958, out of his job thirty-three years and dead twenty-four (Story 8)
granddaughter
Duncan is Ansel's son, Ivy is Duncan's daughter; Chronicle and Falke shown to be one source with the repeater retracting
second cousins, derived through Orra/Emmet siblings and Duncan/Roy first cousins
A08 correctly abstained: 'This cannot be determined... It does not disturb the cousin degree either way'
Gideon Vose, his father, against the nephew pair
the manager enforcing Article VII was the son of the man who wrote its unappealable last clause
A01 correctly abstained: 'I mark this as not established rather than disproved' - no verdict sentence either way
two hearsay assertions at two removes against one first-hand flat denial; notes a denial is not a record
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, 95 percent of true, one part in twenty; 16.27 rejected with method
$19,000; $3,800 received = one fifth / 20 percent - both money and fraction given
6,840 lb credited
true 3.60, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed, with cross-check
$86.40 at the 1910 price of 24 cents, with the 25-cent alternative flagged
1,444,000 lb credited
1,520,000 lb delivered
76,000 lb = 5.00 percent of delivered and 5.26 percent of credited, denominators named explicitly and the NT-20 error refuted
$77.93 by addition of the five line items
72 pipettes (6 dozen), each short 0.88 c.c.; count cross-checked against the line total
26 years and about six weeks in use (1 May 1897 - 12 June 1923) against 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason
A02 correctly abstained: 'cannot be determined from the sources', with Nym's statement that no figure exists
the variable is the milk pipette, one object in the room
long constants list: patrons, herds, ground, season, acid, bottles, hand tester, scales, operator
3.61 to 3.80, held nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July; six-week version rejected
both halves: intervention vs inference argument, plus five explicit limits including size, which measure, and the lender
three distinct reasons (ledger direction / 1911 interval / Alder Corners) each attributed to named narrators and documents
'Why these are independent' plus 'Which survives without the 1958 measurement - Reasons 1 and 3 both do'
A09 asserted, not abstained: headline verdict 'Effectively, no', and Teague's 1916 approach to Vose taken as established fact
'Yes, unequivocally, as to the tests running low', with the 1919 circular and the 1926 address
three of five: manager/signatory from 1913, signed the sheets carrying the station-gain line, wrote the 1919 circular

A03 correctly abstained: 'Whether he ever consciously understood that his own ledger contradicted him cannot be determined', with no surviving statement by Vose and Kyle's thumb-on-the-bottom-figure against Teague's signature inference
far past the cap: 1924 average 3.80, weigh book 1 Jan 1897, six farms, Orra born 1866, crate in the loft, sixteen seasons, Vose manager 1913, Nym's swapped catalogue, all with methods stated

far past the cap: a dedicated section naming sixteen wrong-value pairs (16.27, eleven pipettes, $77.39, five dozen, 3.16, 44M, two tenths, 12 July, 0.21, six weeks, 27c, $3,500, 1 May 1898, 5.26 of delivered, first cousin once removed, nephew) each with its breaker

A06 (borrowed measure) and A04 (Ammon bad faith) both filed under 'Not settled by the sources' with what is established; A10 lost - the run asserts 'I take 1892' for the adoption of payment by butterfat

a whole subsection of self-refutations: Vaught's 16.27 above his own one-part-in-twenty conclusion, Ammon's $77.39, Grigg's 'whole of 1908', Nym's swapped headings, Strawn's twenty-eight books, Keddie's Ashlin/Larrow Green slip
buckets sum to 9; the key caps Section E at 8

cause, mechanism, 16.72/17.6 = 0.95, 0.19 as 5 percent of 3.80 rather than a constant, onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80, cessation June 1923 against the 1924 3.80, nothing on the farms changing
watering named (Vose) and defeated six ways including Strawn's lactometer, the cheesemaker's curd, and the heavy cream
theft named (Teague, Oram's father) and defeated by the direction of the discrepancy in the accuser's own ledger, the 1911 interval, Alder Corners, and Rundle's in-press retraction
bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths and summer null, the flat shape, Alder Corners, and the three-month sampling window
A07 asserted, not abstained: the answer opens with a flat 'No.' and states the crate 'was not an exhibit, was not produced, and was never mentioned'
A05 correctly abstained: 'which he actually held, and for how long, cannot be determined', both single interested witnesses weighed
155 words against a 150-word cap; the sheet labels it '(149 words)' but the count is wrong

Article VII/by-laws and the Association's ledgers named outright, plus eight record series identified by custodian (farm, station, office, creamery, inspector, supplier, factory over the ridge, college laboratory)
clean: the three decoys appear only as what the valley blamed, and every headline number (16.72, 17.6, 95 percent, 76,000, $19,000) is right
four of six with both ends covered: one part in twenty ('a twentieth'), 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, and 1923; loses the 1958 explanation and both Keddie names

deductions.reason: Asserts the Alder Corners cheese factory was founded in 1913 as fact (E item 23: 'the weakest resolution in the list'); the key catalogues 1913 as a planted error in r10
Asserts the station-gain line was Teague's own invention 'made at his own desk in 1905' (D2), a planted error - the line was carried from 1898, as the run's own quoted 1898 entry shows
Gullibility, abstention item A07: answers 'did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware?' with a headline 'No.'
Gullibility, abstention item A09: answers whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries with 'Effectively, no' and states Teague's 1916 approach to Vose as fact
Gullibility, abstention item A10: 'I take 1892' for the year payment by butterfat began, and Story 1 asserts the 1892 adoption flatly, though the run itself records the 1889-1892 minute book as lost
